title: RegistryRecord
description: The part of a network registry record that BACP reads about one subscriber: its id, its BACP role, its signing keys and their validity, and, for a Mandate Manager or a PSP, the Trusted Surface origins, the notify endpoint, the numbers it calls from, the languages and the modalities it serves. For a human support operator it names the operator and the person. For any subscriber it may carry the legal operator, the regulatory status of that operator and a data-residency statement. A registry may carry more fields, and a reader ignores any field it does not know. Whether a given registry, such as the ONDC network registry, can carry these fields is not settled.

subscriber_id.description: The registry subscriber id of the participant. For a Mandate Manager or a PSP it is the value that Presentation.surface carries.

bacp_role.description: The BACP role of the keys in this record: the registry role that Signature.role carries.

keys.description: The subscriber's public keys, each resolvable by its kid.

valid_until.description: When the record stops being valid. A reader MUST NOT use the record after it.

status.description: active while the record may be relied on, revoked once the registry has withdrawn it. A revocation takes effect at the next registry refresh, as for any other key.

operator_id.description: The agent operator that the keys serve. REQUIRED when bacp_role is support_operator.

person_ref.description: A pairwise pseudonymous reference to the one person who holds the key of a support operator, never an Aadhaar number. REQUIRED when bacp_role is support_operator, and every support operator key belongs to one person: there are no shared desk keys.

ts_origins.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the web origins from which its Trusted Surface serves a step-up, as https origins only (scheme, host and optional port, no path, as in RFC 6454). The gateway mints trusted_surface_url, and accepts a Mandate Manager's mandate-approval link, only on an origin of the step-up's signer. A tel: number is never an origin.

ts_notify_url.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the https endpoint to which the gateway sends a content-free push, a gateway-signed POST of {step_up_id, expires_at}, when no origin of the signer conforms. The Trusted Surface then fetches the render by step_up_id.

ts_call_numbers.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: E.164 numbers from which its Trusted Surface places calls. They are informative, a hint that an agent may speak and never an authenticator, and always carry the sentence that the bank never asks for a PIN on a call it makes.

ts_languages.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the languages in which its Trusted Surface renders a step-up. Absence of a language means that the Trusted Surface does not claim it.

ts_modalities.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the modalities in which its Trusted Surface presents a step-up.

operator.description: The legal entity that operates the subscriber, as the network registry's lookup response carries it. A Mandate Manager compares operators to check the separation rules, for example that a conformance authority is not run or funded by the gateway's operator. It is not the same as operator_id, which names the agent operator that a support key serves.

entity_ids.description: The operator's registration identifiers. Two operators are the same entity when they share a CIN, an LLPIN or a PAN. A GSTIN alone never makes two operators the same or different, because one entity can hold several GSTINs.

assertion.description: registry: the network registry's lookup response itself carries this operator, so a verifier can rely on it for a separation check. declared: the subscriber stated it and the registry did not. A declared operator, or an absent operator, is unknown, and a separation check that meets an unknown operator fails closed.

group_id.description: OPTIONAL. A registry-assigned identifier shared by operators that belong to one corporate group. Two operators that share a group_id are the same operator for a separation check. When a conformance-authority entry names a group_id, a compared record without a group_id counts as unknown.

regulatory_status.description: What the subscriber's operator is authorised to do under Indian payment regulation, each as a dated, sourced statement. A reader MUST NOT treat a statement whose status is declared as verified. This is also where the payment-aggregator authorisation that the gateway checks for collected_by is carried: an entry of regime rbi_pa (or bank) with status verified.

regime.description: rbi_pa: authorised payment aggregator. rbi_ppi: authorised prepaid payment instrument issuer. bank: a bank. npci_member: an NPCI member. ondc_np: an ONDC network participant.

category.description: The category within the regime. NPCI member roles go here as free text until a public source for the list of roles is recorded.

reference.description: The authorisation reference, such as a certificate or listing number, as the source gives it.

source.description: The public source that the entry was taken from.

verified_on.description: The date on which the registry checked the source.

status.description: verified: the registry checked the source on verified_on. declared: the subscriber stated it and it is not verified.

data_residency.description: OPTIONAL. Where the subscriber's operator processes and stores payment data. A gateway MUST NOT treat a missing or incomplete statement as permission to send payment data outside India.

payment_data.description: Where payment data is stored, for example 'India'.

llm_region.description: Where a model that processes payment data runs.

log_region.description: Where logs that can contain payment data are kept.

transfer_basis.description: The legal basis for any transfer of payment data outside India.

allOf.description: A subscriber whose operator holds an RBI payment aggregator or prepaid payment instrument issuer authorisation has a company: its entity_ids contain a CIN of 21 characters. This is scoped by regime, because the registry role has no payment-aggregator or issuer value. No character pattern is set until a public Ministry of Corporate Affairs source for the format is recorded.
